claims.text: Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering temperatures above 2300 °C.
Conventionally sintered ZrB2 typically has a relatively porous microstructure.
SPS at approximately 1800 °C can produce fully densified, single-phase ZrB2.
Using SPS can lower the ZrB2 preparation temperature from above 2300 °C to approximately 1800 °C.
The proposed SPS treatment uses high uniaxial pressure, pulsed electric current, and an inert atmosphere.
SPS provides rapid densification and grain refinement while minimizing intergranular porosity in ZrB2.
Pulsed-current-assisted mass transport is responsible for the proposed densification and microstructural refinement.
The combination of a pulsed electric field and high pressure enhances diffusion and mass transport at lower temperatures.
Enhanced diffusion and mass transport yield a uniform, low-porosity ZrB2 microstructure.
A refined, low-porosity microstructure reduces defect-nucleation sites for liquid plating bath attack.
Reducing defect-nucleation sites will reduce bath-induced holes and eventual component failure.
SPS-prepared ZrB2 will have density comparable to or greater than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
SPS-prepared ZrB2 will have mechanical strength comparable to or greater than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
SPS-prepared ZrB2 will have lower porosity than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
SPS-prepared ZrB2 will develop fewer holes during prolonged liquid plating bath exposure than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
Conventionally sintered ZrB2 has greater susceptibility to degradation in liquid plating environments.
The pressure, pulse profile, and holding time required to consistently achieve full densification and phase purity remain to be optimized.
A controlled comparison of SPS and conventional samples can test density, porosity, microstructure, hardness, fracture toughness, and bath-induced hole formation.
